name: Charge pump · doubler, op-amp (no chip)
description: ⚠ Built from textbook circuits, not documented: values chosen here and checked in simulation only, not a tested build. A voltage doubler built from parts, no pump chip, to see how one works: an op-amp square-wave oscillator (IC1, R1–R4, C1, about 22 kHz) pushes C2 up and down; D1 fills C2 from V+ while the square wave is low, and when it goes high C2's top rises to about V+ + 6 V and D2 passes that charge to C3. About 14.6 V from 9 V at 1 mA (less than a chip's 17.5 V: the TL071 doesn't swing rail to rail and the diodes drop a little each). Label the stages it powers VDBL. Values are ordinary starting values, checked in simulation, not a published circuit. The DC readouts don't include the pumping (they show VDBL near V+); the Scope and audio renders do.

notes.part:IC1: The oscillator: the op-amp flips its output between high and low (about 1.5 V and 7.5 V from 9 V, a TL071 doesn't reach its rails) about 22,000 times a second. A TL071, a single op-amp (half of a TL072 is the same); any op-amp works, a rail-to-rail one swings further and pumps higher. Supply: the op-amp's V+ pin is the oscillator's supply, fed from the pedal's V+ (the DC jack or the battery, through the input filter). It draws its current in short pulses at its switching rate; a bulk electrolytic on V+ (10-100 µF, such as the Input filter block's 47 Ω and 100 µF) supplies them close by, so they don't travel back along V+ and whine in the other stages. A pedal that already has one on V+ needs no second cap here (one close to the op-amp helps a little on a long board). A pedal with none, such as a bare battery fuzz like the Rangemaster, needs one: the "Supply without a bulk capacitor" warning says so.
notes.part:R1: R1 and R2 hold IC1's + input at half of V+...
notes.part:R2: ...and R3 nudges it up when the output is high and down when it's low (hysteresis): the two points where IC1 flips.
notes.part:R3: Hysteresis: feeds the output back to the + input, so IC1 snaps cleanly from one state to the other.
notes.part:R4: Timing: charges and discharges C1 from the output. R4 × C1 sets the frequency; double either and it halves (into the audio band: you'd hear it).
notes.part:C1: Timing: when its voltage crosses the + input's flip point, the output flips and C1 heads the other way. A square wave comes out of IC1.
notes.part:C2: The flying capacitor: charged to about V+ through D1 while the square wave is low, then lifted by it when it goes high, so its top sits above V+.
notes.part:D1: Lets V+ fill C2 while the square wave is low; blocks C2's charge from flowing back into V+ when it's lifted.
notes.part:D2: Passes C2's lifted charge on to C3 when the square wave is high; stops C3 draining back when it's low. Schottky (1N5817) for a low drop.
notes.part:C3: Reservoir: holds VDBL up between pushes. Bigger means less ripple.
notes.net:VDBL: About V+ plus the square wave's swing, less two diode drops: 14.6 V from 9 V at 1 mA, falling as you draw more.
